items.title: Ethiopia 'fears Tigray conflict could get out of control'
items.description: Airstrikes and artillery fire rocked northern Ethiopia's Tigray region overnight into Monday, aid sources said, in clashes between federal government and rebel forces that have raised fears of wider fighting. items.title: Tigray war may spill over to Eritrea — helped by Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's rhetoric
items.description: Ethiopia's Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed is consolidating power, but he must contend with a regional alliance opposing him and a Tigray conflict that could spill over into Eritrea.

items.title: How Palestinian reporters defied Israel’s genocide to redefine journalism
items.description: Western media under scrutiny for promoting Israeli narrative rather than standing up for vulnerable journalists in Gaza.

items.title: Ship Sunk Off Bulgaria’s Economic Zone in Latest Black Sea Drone Attack
items.description: Two commercial ships were hit by drones off Bulgaria on Tuesday, with one sinking and its crew missing. items.title: 2 Killed in Massive Ukrainian Drone Attack on Moscow
items.description: Exiled outlet Astra also reported that one of the attacks targeted the Moscow region’s largest fuel storage hub.

items.title: Fort Hood shooter to be executed by firing squad - a first for US military since World War Two
items.description: Nidal Malik Hasan killed 13 unarmed soldiers and injured another 32 in the deadliest ever non-combat attack on an American military base.

items.title: Three years after October 7: Despite pain, two former Hamas hostages promote message of peace
items.description: Among the 251 Israelis taken captive by Hamas on October 7, 2023, Aviva and Keith Siegel chose to speak publicly about the abuse they suffered. While Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has claimed the release of hostages as an achievement in his election campaign, the couple in their 60s has continued to oppose the war.

items.title: Drones buzz overhead, troops hunker underground in Ukraine's hellish kill zone
items.description: The front line in the Russia-Ukraine war stretches more than 700 miles and has barely moved in four years. Yet straddling this line is the kill zone, dominated by constantly evolving drone technology.

items.title: Sudan: Driver killed in aerial attack on aid trucks in South Kordofan
items.description: The World Food Programme (WFP) has strongly condemned a deadly airstrike on two clearly marked aid trucks in South Kordofan, Sudan, this past weekend.

items.title: Ukrainian Singer Returns Home From US To Perform For Ukrainian Soldiers Near Front Line
items.description: After studying at Berklee and building a career in New York, Ukrainian singer Valeriia Vovk returned home to perform for troops, including near the front. She says simply being there, talking to soldiers and singing for them, has great value.
